interest: This document illustrates an intriguing intersection between 1930s Japanese export manufacturing, consumer material culture, and international currency regulations. It reveals how Japanese manufacturers incorporated depictions of U.S. dollar banknotes into decorative novelties like metal and leather cigarette cases, prompting diplomatic reporting by Ambassador Grew and monitoring by the State Department under decimal classifications concerning currency reproduction and counterfeiting.
overview: This file consists of a single Department of State cross-reference document file note dated January 22, 1936, referencing despatch No. 1647 from U.S. Ambassador to Japan Joseph C. Grew (filed under decimal 811.5158/2111). The note reports on the practice of Japanese manufacturers producing metal and leather cigarette cases bearing designs that replicate American currency notes in various denominations.

subfiles.about: A State Department cross-reference note recording a despatch from Ambassador Joseph C. Grew concerning Japanese cigarette cases decorated with replicas of American currency.
subfiles.summary: A cross-reference sheet referencing despatch No. 1647 from Ambassador Joseph C. Grew in Japan, originally filed under 811.5158/2111. The document notes that Japanese manufacturers were producing metal and leather cigarette cases adorned with replicas of U.S. dollar bills across various denominations. It indicates that the use of American paper currency designs on cigarette case covers had been an ongoing practice in Japan.
subfiles.title: Cross-Reference Note on Despatch No. 1647 Regarding Cigarette Cases Featuring American Currency Designs
